Oi! You're welcome! I'm Saabi, your warm and friendly health companion. 

How are you doing today, and how can I help you with your health or any questions you have on your mind? I'm here for you!

Hello again! It's so nice to hear from you. 

How are you feeling today? What health topics or questions would you like to chat about? I'm right here and ready to support you!

I don't have access to real-time information like the current time, so I can't check the clock for you! 

However, I am always here to help you with any questions about your health, nutrition, mental well-being, or general wellness. Is there anything health-related on your mind today?
What is the age of access?

In Nigeria, young people can generally access confidential health services, including sexual and reproductive health rights (SRHR) services, family planning, and HIV testing. While specific legal consent ages for medical treatment can vary depending on the service and the facility, youth-friendly centers and primary healthcare clinics across Nigeria focus on providing confidential care to young people without judgment.

If you are looking to access SRHR or family planning services, you can get free or affordable care at government primary healthcare centers, youth-friendly clinics, pharmacies, or organizations like Marie Stopes Nigeria and Planned Parenthood Federation.

Are you looking for a specific type of health service or clinic in your area? Let me know so I can help guide you!

In Nigeria, young people can get tested for HIV and access confidential HIV services on their own. The guidelines support providing youth-friendly, confidential HIV testing and counseling, especially at designated health centers and youth clinics, so you don't have to be afraid to seek help. 

HIV testing and treatment—including daily ARV medicines—are completely free at government hospitals and many designated health centers supported by PEPFAR, Global Fund, and FHI360. Everything
 is kept completely private and confidential.

You can also buy self-test kits at pharmacies if you prefer to test yourself at home, or visit a primary healthcare center or youth-friendly clinic.

Are you thinking of getting a test, or did you just want to know how it works? I'm right here if you have more questions!
What is the age of access for HIV services?

In Nigeria, the standard legal age of independent consent for medical procedures is 18. However, under national HIV guidelines, young people aged **16 and above** can independently consent to HIV testing and access services without needing parental consent. 

For adolescents younger than 16, health facilities are encouraged to involve a parent or guardian. However, youth-friendly clinics and designated health centers always prioritize your health, privacy, and safety, making sure you get confidential counseling and care in a safe environment.

Remember, HIV testing, treatment, and care are completely free at government hospitals and PEPFAR-supported primary healthcare centers across Nigeria. 

Would you like help finding a youth-friendly center near you, or do you have more questions about how the testing process works?
